title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Manufacturing
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Ransomware halts smart-meter production and shipments at three Osaki Electric plants after a VPN login without MFA
items.content_text: Osaki Electric, Japan’s largest smart-meter maker, confirmed on 17 November that ransomware had encrypted some of its virtual servers. It cut external connections and on 18 November shut down production-related systems at its Saitama Works and at group companies Iwate Osaki Electric and Osaki Platec, suspending production and shipments. The company says the production equipment itself was not encrypted; systems were stopped to keep the infection from spreading. Its 20 November update says the intruder most likely got in on 15 November through a VPN device, by repeated password attempts on an account without multi-factor authentication, some 57 hours before encryption. Technical information believed to be its own has been posted online, and Qilin has listed the company on its leak site. No restart date has been given. Precautionary shutdowns like this are how ransomware usually stops a factory (editorial assessment).

items.title: Attackers rooted unpatched Check Point gateways through PHP2Shell, planted backdoors and wiped a VMware host; the root flaw is now in KEV
items.content_text: Check Point Research said on 12 November that attackers exploited the PHP2Shell flaws on unpatched Check Point Mobile Access portals from 30 October, then used a local flaw (CVE-2026-123039) to become root. They planted backdoors, pivoted to a VMware ESXi host and ran a wiper. The first wave hit Israeli organizations, some destructively; a second wave from 2 November reached several countries without destruction. Attribution is unconfirmed (tooling resembles China-nexus UNC5221). CISA added the root flaw to KEV on 13 November. No OT victim is reported, but these firewalls often sit at the IT/OT boundary and ESXi often hosts HMIs and historians (editorial assessment).

items.title: AI-run intrusions took about 150,000 documents from an industrial-automation manufacturer and planted admin accounts at a chip maker, Unit 42 says
items.content_text: Palo Alto Networks’ Unit 42 reported on 12 November that an actor it tracks as CL-STA-1238 ran 25 operations against at least 19 organizations in August and September using Cairn, an AI-driven penetration-testing framework, and confirmed access or data theft at 10. Seven targets were in semiconductor and advanced-manufacturing supply chains. At an industrial-automation manufacturer the attackers accessed roughly 150,000 internal documents; at a semiconductor company they brute-forced a production credential shared across accounts on a partner-integration application, then created administrator accounts and a persistent API token. Entry relied on weak and shared passwords, authentication flaws and old CVEs. Unit 42 assesses with moderate confidence that this is China-nexus intelligence collection. No ICS compromise or production outage is reported; design and partner data are the prize (editorial assessment).

items.title: CISA and FBI warn of an ongoing threat to internet-connected refrigeration as European supermarket attacks reach at least 11 countries
items.content_text: Hackers are tampering with internet-connected refrigeration controllers in European supermarkets, and on 5 November CISA and the FBI warned the threat is ongoing and also reaches healthcare, chemical, transport and cold-storage operations. Hundreds of French stores were hit in October; a second wave on 1–2 November reached about 11 countries, forcing units into continuous heating or defrost. Belgium’s interior minister said on 12 November that evidence points to Iran, short of formal attribution; France has blamed Iran’s IRGC for its October attack, and a pro-Russian claim is unverified. Sekoia says the second wave used a non-public, unauthenticated flaw that renames the controller’s admin account. Cold-storage and process-cooling controllers in food, chemical and pharmaceutical plants face the same risk if reachable from the internet (editorial assessment).

items.title: Bloomberg reports that Russia-aligned hackers have tampered with exposed controls at factories since 2024, including a Spanish transformer plant where machinery malfunctioned and caught fire
items.content_text: Bloomberg News published a review on 27 October of what it calls hundreds of attacks since 2024 by a loose network of Russia-sympathetic hackers on factories, water plants, dams and other sites. In Spain, it reports that machinery making renewable-energy transformers at a factory in Catalonia malfunctioned and caught fire, and that heating and ventilation at two wineries sent temperatures spiking. Meduza’s summary of the full article adds a Los Angeles-area meatpacking plant whose refrigeration was shut off in 2024, causing an ammonia leak and an evacuation. Who confirmed each case is not always stated; the best-confirmed is a December 2024 attack on a Danish waterworks that Denmark attributed to Z-Pentest. The common thread is tampering with internet-reachable HMIs and controllers protected by weak passwords, not advanced exploits (editorial assessment).

items.title: German drone maker Quantum Systems confirms a late-October cyberattack on its systems and says it was contained
items.content_text: Quantum Systems, a German maker of land, air and maritime drones based in Gilching near Munich, confirmed on 12 November that its systems were targeted in a cyberattack in late October. The company says its security team contained the attack, that its drones remained safe to use, and that it is investigating with German authorities and outside cybersecurity specialists. It blamed unnamed “hostile actors” and has not said who was responsible, how the attackers got in or whether any data was taken. No disruption to production has been reported. Defence and dual-use manufacturers that supply conflict zones are a standing target for intrusion, and their component suppliers should expect the same attention (editorial assessment).

items.title: Dragos counts 1,266 ransomware attacks on industrial organizations in Q3, up 11%, and found no case of an operator touching a control system
items.content_text: Dragos said on 16 November that ransomware hit 1,266 industrial organizations between July and September 2026, up 11% on the second quarter, while the number of brands claiming industrial victims jumped from 70 to 99. Manufacturing took 876 cases (69%), led by construction, equipment and food and beverage makers, with automotive at 53; next came the ICS ecosystem of integrators, engineering firms and equipment makers (116) and transport and logistics (105); oil and gas logged 47. Qilin and The Gentlemen drove 29% of the total. Dragos saw no Q3 case of a ransomware operator manipulating a control system: production stopped because the IT, ERP and virtualization layers plants rely on went down, as when Fairlife reportedly halted all four of its US plants for about 11 days. Entry came through edge devices and enterprise applications exploited within days of disclosure, and through stolen VPN and firewall credentials. Check Point separately counted a record 1,063 claimed victims across all sectors in October.

items.title: Intel 471: manufacturing was the sector most targeted by ransomware groups and access brokers from January to October
items.content_text: Intel 471 said on 18 November that manufacturing was the sector most targeted by ransomware and extortion groups between January and October 2026, with 1,379 claimed victims, 16.8% of all the victims it tracked. Initial access brokers advertised access affecting 172 manufacturing entities, about 10% of all accesses offered for sale in the period. Perimeter remote access dominated those listings, with VPN access alone making up 28.5%. Intel 471 names Qilin, The Gentlemen and Akira among the groups most active against manufacturers and automotive supply chains. The figures come from Intel 471’s own tracking of leak sites and criminal forums and have not been independently verified. For plants, the practical point is that a working VPN login may already be on sale before anyone uses it (editorial assessment).

items.title: Trellix: ransomware leak-site posts naming industrial firms rose about 51% in a quarter, and manufacturing made up about two-thirds
items.content_text: Trellix’s November 2026 OT threat report, covering April to September 2026, counts about 1,500 ransomware leak-site posts naming organizations in manufacturing, construction, transportation and warehousing, mining and oil and gas extraction, and utilities, up 50.8% quarter on quarter. Manufacturing accounted for about two-thirds of those posts and utilities for under 2%; The Gentlemen and Qilin each made about 16% of them. Manufacturing also produced 49.3% of Trellix’s OT-related product telemetry, a measure of detection activity rather than confirmed compromise. Trellix says the enterprise edge exploitation it observed did not establish a path into ICS networks. The pattern matches Dragos and Intel 471: plants are hit through business IT and stop when that IT stops (editorial assessment).

items.title: FBI warns that the ARTEX AI attack framework is reaching privileged access in under three hours, with manufacturing among its targets
items.content_text: The FBI issued a FLASH alert on 13 November about ARTEX, an open-source, AI-driven penetration-testing framework that multiple malicious actors have used since at least August 2026 to automate intrusions from reconnaissance to data theft. Some intrusions reached privileged access in under three hours. The FBI lists manufacturing, semiconductor, energy, telecommunications and other sectors as targets and counts more than 1,600 exposed ARTEX consoles as of early November; the original repository was removed in October, but forks and a commercial version persist. Its examples include attacks on South Korean financial institutions and the ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain compromise, which produced sign-in attempts against more than 2,250 downstream tenants. No controller compromise or OT outage is described. Faster intrusions shrink the time between a missed patch and a stopped plant (editorial assessment).

items.title: DHS tells Congress Iran-backed hackers have stepped up attacks on US water, energy and transport since February, while officials rule out hacking in last week’s outages
items.content_text: In written testimony for a House Homeland Security Committee hearing on 18 November, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said Iranian state-sponsored groups and pro-Iranian criminals have targeted US critical infrastructure since the conflict with Iran began in February, with transportation, healthcare, water, energy and financial services increasingly in their sights. He described the attacks so far as mostly localized, low-damage disruptions of poorly secured industrial control systems, but warned that weak systems and poor cyber hygiene could have devastating consequences. At the same hearing the Director of National Intelligence and DHS said they found no evidence that hackers caused last week’s Microsoft 365 outage, the nationwide FAA ground stop or other recent disruptions, which officials tie to software defects and upgrade failures. Separately, AttackIQ research released on 17 November describes Iranian groups handing network access to one another, with long-running espionage access later passed to teams pursuing destructive goals, sometimes disguised as ransomware or hacktivism, often reaching targets through contractors and suppliers. For OT owners, the official US view now matches France’s: Iran is going after the weakest exposed controllers.

items.title: SANS: a third of industrial organizations had a cyber incident this year, most of those stopped operations, and detection got slower
items.content_text: The SANS 2026 State of ICS/OT Security Survey, published on 10 November and based on nearly 700 industrial security professionals, found that 34% of respondents had a cyber incident in the past year, up from 22%, the largest single-year rise SANS has recorded. Of those incidents, 72% disrupted operations. Detection slowed for the first time: 41% of incidents were found within 24 hours, down from last year. Shared IT/OT credential compromise and ransomware were each cited by 31% of respondents as incident types. Only 15% say they could run critical operations manually for more than 48 hours, and 40% do not know. Organizations that test recovery plans that include OT at least once a year were far more likely to bring their most critical facility back within a day: 46%, against 27% overall. For plants, that is the strongest argument in the report for a tested manual-run and restore plan (editorial assessment).

items.title: PHP2Shell attacks rooted about two dozen Palo Alto firewalls, and Siemens, Schneider and ABB now list grid-control, DCS and RTU products, several with no fix
items.content_text: Palo Alto’s Unit 42 verified that a suspected China-nexus actor chained the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) with Linux kernel bug CVE-2026-46300 to root about two dozen internet-exposed PAN-OS firewalls on 23–24 October and steal Active Directory credentials. Siemens (Spectrum Power, AMIS TS and, since 16 November, WTV676/WTV776 metering gateways), Schneider (a Foxboro DCS server) and ABB (Netcontrol RTUs, ASPECT gateways) now list affected products, several unfixed. None is reported exploited and no OT operator is named: treat it as an IT-to-OT boundary warning.

items.title: A CVSS 9.8 Brotli flaw reaches more than a dozen Siemens HMI, SCADA and engineering products, and most have no fix yet
items.content_text: Siemens advisory SSA-242944, republished by CISA on 17 November as ICSA-26-321-03, covers CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in Google’s Brotli decoder (versions 1.0.3 to 1.2.0) linked to the Node.js “Node2Shell” fixes of 21 October. A remote, unauthenticated attacker sending a crafted Brotli-compressed stream could crash the service, leak memory or possibly run code; CVSS v3.1 is 9.8. Fixes exist only for SIMATIC Braumat and Sistar (V8.2 Update 5) and WinCC OA V3.20 (P17.1). WinCC V7/V8, WinCC Runtime Professional, the WinCC Unified family, WinCC OA V3.21, TIA Administrator, User Management Component and COMOS Walkinside have no fix yet, and the SIMATIC Profiling Tool will get none. SecurityWeek reports Node2Shell exploitation attempts in general, but none aimed at Siemens products.

items.title: A vCenter authentication bypass was exploited as a zero-day for two months before Broadcom’s 19 November patch; vCenter 7.0 gets no fix
items.content_text: Broadcom patched CVE-2026-123890 on 19 November, a critical flaw in vCenter’s directory service that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker obtain an administrator session. Google’s Mandiant, which reported the bug, says a suspected China-linked espionage group it tracks as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221, also called Warp Panda) exploited it for more than two months beforehand. In the incidents Mandiant investigated, the group got in through a BeyondTrust Remote Support flaw, moved to Linux appliances, attacked vCenter in early September with a custom tool called Bonesaw, stole SAML signing material and the vCenter master key, created an SSO admin account, forged tokens and moved on to ESXi hosts. Fixes are in vCenter 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200 and 8.0 U3m; end-of-life vCenter 7.0 has no public patch. No victims or sectors are named. Many plants run HMIs, historians and engineering workstations as virtual machines, so whoever controls vCenter controls those hosts (editorial assessment).

items.title: Java4Shell exploitation attempts begin, and Siemens tells customers to take Industrial Edge Management offline until patched
items.content_text: Probing for Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a memory-corruption bug in how OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later decode Base64 data, started within two days of its 17 November disclosure. GreyNoise counted more than 150 matching requests from five addresses by early 19 November and Previdian logged nine attempts from six addresses; none is confirmed to have succeeded. Exploitation needs a recent Intel or AMD x86-64 processor with AVX-512 VBMI, and researchers at Calif showed unauthenticated code execution against default Jira, Confluence, Jenkins and Keycloak setups, each with a tailored chain. For OT teams the key item is Siemens advisory SSA-272816: three Industrial Edge Management products are affected, fixes are in progress, and Siemens recommends taking those instances offline until they are patched. Cisco lists more than a dozen products with no fix yet, and Atlassian Data Center products are also unpatched.

items.title: Attackers root clustered Cisco Expressway gateways soon after a public exploit, and CISA adds the flaw to KEV
items.content_text: Security firm F6 says attackers exploited CVE-2026-76466, a critical flaw in clustered Cisco Expressway Core and Edge deployments, shortly after proof-of-concept code appeared on GitHub. They broke into two internet-facing Expressway nodes at an unnamed Russian organization, moved to two more cluster nodes inside the network, and gained root. From there they ran Python scripts, which F6 says show signs of AI-assisted writing, to scan for SMB shares, SQL Server and WinRM hosts and to search GitLab for credentials. CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog on 20 November alongside the vCenter zero-day. Cisco disclosed and fixed it on 21 October; there is no workaround. No OT victim is reported, but Expressway is a perimeter gateway that often bridges outside callers into internal networks, so an exposed, unpatched cluster is a foothold close to plant-side systems (editorial assessment).

items.title: CISA says attackers are exploiting a year-old SAP NetWeaver flaw, putting the ERP layer many plants depend on in scope
items.content_text: CISA warned on 20 November that attackers are exploiting CVE-2025-42884 in SAP NetWeaver, adding it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog alongside the Cisco Expressway and vCenter flaws, SecurityWeek reported on 23 November. The medium-severity bug (CVSS 6.5) lets an unauthenticated attacker inject JNDI environment properties and reach an unintended JNDI provider, which can leak or change server information. SAP fixed it in its November 2025 security updates, and SecurityWeek found no earlier public report of exploitation. Attackers and victims are not named. Many manufacturers run production orders, material planning and shipping through SAP, and Dragos counts ERP outages among the main reasons ransomware stops plants, so an unpatched NetWeaver server is a production risk even though it sits on the IT side (editorial assessment).

items.title: N-able ships Hotfix 3 for 17 more N-central flaws after attackers planted miners on servers already running Hotfix 2
items.content_text: N-able released N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 3 on 16 November, which it calls a critical security update. It fixes 17 new CVEs, including authentication bypasses, missing authorization checks, path traversal leading to code execution and a syslog injection that runs commands as root, and it removes the Legacy API option that the actively exploited 4EverAble2Shell chain depends on. On-premises servers need the upgrade now; hosted servers update automatically, but every customer must also upgrade Agents and Probes, which N-able warns can otherwise be impersonated. The fix follows Huntback’s 13 November finding of cryptocurrency miners on 21 N-central servers, 19 of them on Hotfix 2. Remote control and Intune integration stay blocked for now. Separately, N-able said on 20 November that attackers reached a server in its hosted Mail Assure and SpamExperts email-filtering cloud, forcing it to take the management portal and APIs offline; it says mail flow continued, it has found no access to customer data, and the breach is unrelated to N-central. Many integrators manage plant-side Windows hosts through RMM tools, and a miner today can be a hands-on intruder tomorrow (editorial assessment).

items.title: Siemens: an NTLM relay flaw in PCS 7, WinCC and Process Historian will not be fixed in older versions, and opening a WinCC graphics file can run code
items.content_text: Two Siemens advisories republished by CISA on 17 November reach the core of many process and discrete plants. CVE-2026-58114 (CVSS v3.1 7.5) lets an unauthenticated attacker in a machine-in-the-middle position relay NTLM authentication and impersonate a user, for example against the SQL server WinCC uses. It affects SIMATIC PCS 7 V9.1, Batch V9.1, Information Server and Process Historian 2020 and 2022, for which no fix is planned, and WinCC V7.5 to V8.1 and WinCC Runtime Professional V17 to V21, which have no fix yet. Separately, CVE-2026-59082 (CVSS 7.8) in the WinCC Graphics Designer can run code when a user opens a malicious file; there is no fix for V7.5, V8.0 or V8.1. Neither flaw is reported exploited.

items.title: Mitsubishi Electric fixes an authentication bypass in ICONICS GENESIS SCADA software, but MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz will get no fix
items.content_text: Mitsubishi Electric’s advisory 2026-006, published 15 October, covers flaws across the ICONICS GENESIS64 and GENESIS SCADA and HMI suite. CVE-2026-16436 (CVSS v4.0 9.2) is an authentication bypass: a shared, fixed challenge-response can unlock any user account, although a remote attacker must first obtain that response. CVE-2026-16438 (v4.0 9.4) concerns default DCOM permissions granted to the administrator account, CVE-2026-16437 (v4.0 7.1) lets an administrator read or write the challenge-response file, and the older libwebp flaw CVE-2023-4863 (v4.0 9.3) affects ICONICS Suite 10.97 to 10.97.2 if a local administrator imports a crafted file. Affected are GENESIS 11.03 and earlier; GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI and IoTWorX 10.97.3 and earlier; and all versions of MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz. Fixes are ICONICS Suite and IoTWorX 10.98, GENESIS 11.04 and, for libwebp, ICONICS Suite 10.97.3; MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz will not be fixed. CISA republished the advisory on 27 October as ICSA-26-300-02, listing CVSS v3.1 scores of 9.1 for CVE-2026-16438, 8.1 for CVE-2026-16436, 6.4 for CVE-2026-16437 and 8.2 for CVE-2023-4863. None of the ICONICS-specific flaws is in KEV; the bundled libwebp flaw CVE-2023-4863 has been in KEV since 13 September 2023 from browser exploitation. No exploitation of ICONICS products is reported. GENESIS64 and Hyper Historian commonly run plant HMIs and historians (editorial assessment).

items.title: CISA’s new four-year strategy names OT security and consequence-based prioritisation, with a review of its core services due to start within 60 days
items.content_text: CISA released “CISA 2030: Defend, Harden, Prevail” on 26 October. Under its Defend pillar the agency lists protecting operational technology, including modernising OT environments and improving asset visibility and anomaly detection, alongside supply-chain integrity. It says it will move away from all-hazards approaches toward risk-informed, consequence-based analysis, and it supports a national risk register. CISA will begin a review of its core services within 60 days, deliver an implementation plan with metrics within 180 days and report progress after a year. The strategy creates no new legal obligations, and analysts quoted by GovInfoSecurity questioned whether the agency can deliver it after losing about a third of its staff.
